title: 15ho7q0
Mu'awiya and Imam Hasan: the peace, its violation, and the poisoning claim
hook: Imam Hasan made peace so that blood would not be shed. Mu'awiya trampled the condition underfoot and had him poisoned.
scenes.0.text: When **Imam Ali** was martyred in Kufa, the people pledged allegiance to **Imam Hasan**. Allegiance is a pledge of loyalty. Imam Hasan, whom the Prophet called sayyid, took on the leadership. His father had not said in his will to hand leadership over to **Mu'awiya**. **Mu'awiya** held the trade routes in Damascus. He was very rich. He marched with a great army. Through trickery, purchase and bribery he bought the commanders. **Ubaydullah b. Abbas** crossed over to **Mu'awiya** at night. The army rotted from within. **Imam Hasan** was left powerless.
scenes.1.text: In Kufa **Imam Hasan** ended the war so that blood would not be shed and the friends of the ==Ahl al-Bayt== would not be destroyed. Leadership passed to **Mu'awiya**. The Prophet had said, "This son of mine is a sayyid. God will reconcile two great groups through him." This peace was not weakness. It was stopping the bloodshed inside a bought army.
scenes.2.text: In the peace made at Kufa the condition was clear. **Mu'awiya** would act by the Book of God and the sunna of the Prophet, would let no one be cursed, and would not appoint a caliph after himself. **Imam Hasan** wanted to protect the honor of the ==Ahl al-Bayt== and the pulpit with this word. The conditions were put in writing. **Mu'awiya** later ==trampled== the terms of this agreement.
scenes.3.text: At Nukhayla, in Kufa, **Mu'awiya** spoke openly. "I did not fight you for prayer or fasting. I fought you to rule over you." He counted the peace conditions as ==under his feet==. There he broke the word **Imam Hasan** had given in order not to shed blood.
scenes.4.text: Right after the peace, **Imam Ali** was cursed from the pulpits. **Hujr b. Adi** and his companions, who refused this, were killed. **Imam Hasan** lived in Medina for ten years. The peace had been broken. Around 50 AH he was poisoned. Mu'awiya, who broke the agreement, also played a part in this poisoning.
scenes.5.text: In Medina **Mu'awiya** gave **Imam Hasan**'s wife **Ja'da bint al-Ash'ath** a promise of marriage to his son **Yazid** and a hundred thousand dirhams. The poison was administered through this bargain. The aim was that the throne would remain with the son. **Mu'awiya** did not keep his promise. Neither was there a marriage nor was the money completed. The Prophet's sayyid was martyred in the order built by the killer of his father. This path leads to the allegiance to **Yazid** at Karbala.
scenes.6.text: In Medina it is reported that **Imam Hasan** was poisoned. "His liver melted" is not a physician's expression. It is the language of pain. Qatada reports that he said his liver was torn to pieces. This is not a word-for-word translation. Ibn Abd al-Barr reports that a group tied the poison to Mu'awiya and does not himself pass judgment. His lovers regarded him as a martyr. The throne was cleared for a son. The greatest of the ==Ahl al-Bayt== had been deceived at the peace table and poisoned in his own home. This is the first great mourning before Karbala.
scenes.7.text: In Medina **Imam Husayn** took his brother **Imam Hasan** to bury him beside his grandfather, the Messenger of God. Imam Hasan had left a will: "Let not a drop of blood be shed at my funeral." If blood was to be shed, he wanted to be buried at Baqi', beside his mother. **Aisha** came riding a mule with **Marwan** and the Umayyads. She personally prevented the coffin from being buried beside the Prophet. "You cannot bring into my house someone I do not love," she said. She also gave the order for arrows to be shot at the coffin. Marwan's men fired on that order. The arrows lodged in the coffin. **Ibn Abbas** said to her, "One day the camel, one day the mule." At the Camel there was the camel, that day there was the mule. **Imam Husayn** did not draw his sword. His brother's will was there. Imam Hasan was buried at Baqi'.
sunni.0.says: The Prophet calling Imam Hasan «sayyid» and the saying «He will reconcile two great groups».
sunni.1.says: They do not regard the report of Mu'awiya's promise to Ja'da as established; they relate the poisoning as an event.
sunni.2.says: The conditions of the peace, Mu'awiya's entry into Kufa, and the Year of Unity.
shia.0.says: The poisoning, Ja'da, and Mu'awiya's promise.
shia.1.says: The peace conditions, Mu'awiya's speech at Nukhayla, and the poisoning.
shia.2.says: Mu'awiya's view of the conditions and the reasons for Imam Hasan's peace.
shia.3.says: It is related that Aisha personally prevented the coffin from being buried beside the Prophet and gave the order to shoot arrows, that Marwan's men fired on this order, Ibn Abbas's saying about the camel and the mule, and that Imam Husayn buried him at Baqi' without drawing his sword. A page number was not given separately.
shia.4.says: It is told that Imam Hasan's commander Ubaydullah b. Abbas crossed over to Mu'awiya at night. A page number was not given separately.
shia.5.says: The peace conditions and Mu'awiya's failure to keep them.
disputes.0.title: 1jf3g0w
Who poisoned Imam Hasan?
disputes.0.sunni: There are many sources that tell of Imam Hasan's being poisoned. Some Sunni scholars do not regard Mu'awiya's order as established; it is also said that the death may have been from illness.
disputes.0.shia: There are many sources that tell of Imam Hasan's being poisoned. Among Shia books, Mufid, Kulayni and Tabarsi relate that Mu'awiya persuaded Ja'da to do this.
disputes.1.title: q0e65r
Were the peace conditions kept?
disputes.1.sunni: It is agreed that Imam Hasan gave up the leadership so that blood would not be shed. The text of the conditions varies; practices such as cursing can be considered to have damaged the spirit of the peace.
disputes.1.shia: It is agreed that Imam Hasan gave up the leadership so that blood would not be shed. In the Shia account, Mu'awiya accepted the conditions intending from the start to break them.
questions.0: As Imam Hasan's army was dissolving, he chose to stop the blood. How does this peace look to you as a sacrifice?
questions.1: After the peace, cursing spread from the pulpits and the succession of a crown prince came onto the agenda. What does the difference between Imam Hasan's intention and the later practices tell you?
questions.2: An event appears in many books, while the perpetrator remains disputed. How do you think calmly in such a place?
summary: Mu'awiya was rich through the trade routes of Damascus. He bought Ubaydullah b. Abbas and the commanders. Imam Hasan ended the war so that blood would not be shed. Mu'awiya trampled the conditions of the peace. Imam Hasan died poisoned around 50 AH.
key: The conditions of the peace and the poisoning of Imam Hasan
notes.0: Mu'awiya was rich through the trade routes of Damascus. He bought the army with bribes. Ubaydullah b. Abbas crossed over to him at night. Imam Hasan ended the war so that blood would not be shed. Mu'awiya later trampled the peace conditions.
notes.1: Among the peace conditions are counted not letting anyone be cursed and not appointing a caliph.
notes.2: It is reported that Mu'awiya said at Nukhayla "I fought you to rule over you" (should be checked against the source).
notes.3: Imam Hasan died poisoned around 50 AH.
notes.4: That Imam Hasan was poisoned is told in the history books; Ja'da's name is mentioned. In the Ja'fari school this is his martyrdom.
